intro.text: Commercial Vehicle Group, Inc. and its subsidiaries, is a global provider of systems, assemblies and components to global commercial vehicle markets and electric vehicle markets. We deliver real solutions to complex design, engineering and manufacturing problems while creating positive change for our customers, industries, and communities we serve. References herein to the "Company", "CVG", "we", "our", or "us" refer to Commercial Vehicle Group, Inc. and its subsidiaries. We have manufacturing operations in the United States, Mexico, China, United Kingdom, Czech Republic, Ukraine, Morocco, Thailand, India and Australia. Our products are primarily sold in North America, Europe, and the Asia-Pacific region.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: In addition, as of December 31, 2025, receivables from our top five customers represented approximately 46% of total receivables.

We have operations in the Mexico, China, United Kingdom, Czech Republic, Morocco, Ukraine, Australia, India and Thailand, which collectively accounted for approximately 38% of our total revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025.
As of December 31, 2025, receivables from our top five customers represented approximately 46 % of total receivables.
Sales to two of our customers were individually in excess of 10% of total Company revenues in each of the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, as noted in the table below.
Customer A | Global Seats and Trim Systems & Components | 13% | 13% | 13%
We generally are not dependent on a single supplier or limited group of suppliers for our raw materials.
We rely on third parties for raw materials, parts, and components.
Our ability to make payments on our indebtedness depends on our ability to generate cash in the future.
We rely on technology for the operation of our business.

Cost of revenues decreased $69.6 million, or 10.7% as a result of a decrease in raw material and purchased component costs of $46.8 million, or 12.3%; a decrease in wages and benefits of $4.3 million, or 6.9%; and a decrease in overhead expenses of $18.4 million, or 8.9%.

Cost of revenues decreased $64.1 million, or 9.0% as a result of a decrease in raw material and purchased component costs of $54.9 million, or 12.6%; a decrease in wages and benefits of $6.9 million, or 9.9%; and a decrease in overhead expens es of $2.3 million, or 1.1%.
Our primary sources of liquidity during the year ended December 31, 2025 were operating income, cash and availability under our credit facility.
We also rely on the timely collection of receivables as a source of liquidity.
The realization of a deferred tax asset ultimately depends on the existence of sufficient taxable income in either the carryback or carryforward periods under tax law.
On July 24, 2023, one of our customers issued a voluntary safety recall related to certain wiper system components supplied by us.
